**Rochdale Town Hall** is a [Victorian-era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_era "Victorian era")[municipal building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_and_town_halls "City and town halls") in [Rochdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale "Rochdale"), [Greater Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Manchester "Greater Manchester"), England. It is "widely recognised as being one of the finest municipal buildings in the country",[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-RMBC43-4) and is recorded in the [National Heritage List for England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Heritage_List_for_England "National Heritage List for England") as a designated Grade I [listed building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Listed_building#England_and_Wales "Listed building"). The town hall functions as the ceremonial headquarters of [Rochdale Metropolitan Borough Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Borough_of_Rochdale "Metropolitan Borough of Rochdale") and houses local government departments, including the borough's [civil registration office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_registry "Civil registry").

Built in the [Gothic Revival style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_Revival_architecture "Gothic Revival architecture") at a cost of £160,000 (£16.3 million in 2025),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-inflation-UK-7) it was inaugurated for the governance of the [Municipal Borough of Rochdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Borough_of_Rochdale "County Borough of Rochdale") on 27 September 1871. The architect, [William Henry Crossland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Henry_Crossland "William Henry Crossland"), was the winner of a competition held in 1864 to design a new town hall. It had a 240-foot (73 m)[clock tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clock_tower "Clock tower") topped by a wooden spire with a gilded statue of [Saint George and the Dragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_George_and_the_Dragon "Saint George and the Dragon"), both of which were destroyed by fire on 10 April 1883, leaving the building without a spire for four years. A new 190-foot (58 m) stone clock tower and spire in the style of [Manchester Town Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Town_Hall "Manchester Town Hall") was designed by [Alfred Waterhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Waterhouse "Alfred Waterhouse"), and erected in 1887.

Architectural historian [Nikolaus Pevsner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolaus_Pevsner "Nikolaus Pevsner") described the building as possessing a "rare picturesque beauty".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Pevsner_59-8) Its [stained-glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stained-glass "Stained-glass") windows are credited as "the finest modern examples of their kind".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-RMBC43-4) It is suggested that the building came to the attention of [Adolf Hitler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Hitler "Adolf Hitler"), who was said to have admired it so much that he wished to ship the building, brick-by-brick, to [Nazi Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany") had the United Kingdom been defeated in the Second World War. However, there is little concrete evidence available to support this claim.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-9)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale_Town_Hall&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Rochdale had developed into an increasingly large, populous, and prosperous urban [mill town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mill_town "Mill town") since the [Industrial Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_Revolution "Industrial Revolution"). Its newly built rail and canal network, and numerous factories, resulted in the town being "remarkable for many wealthy merchants".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Roch7-10) In January 1856, the electorate of the [Rochdale constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_(UK_Parliament_constituency) "Rochdale (UK Parliament constituency)") petitioned the [Privy Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her_Majesty's_Most_Honourable_Privy_Council "Her Majesty's Most Honourable Privy Council") for the grant of a [charter of incorporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_charter "Royal charter") under the [Municipal Corporations Act 1835](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_Corporations_Act_1835 "Municipal Corporations Act 1835"), to constitute the town as a [municipal borough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_borough "Municipal borough"). This would give it limited political autonomy via an elected town council, comprising a mayor, [aldermen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alderman "Alderman"), and [councillors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Councillor "Councillor"), to oversee local affairs.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-lg21845-11) The petition was successful and the charter was granted in September 1856.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-12) The newly formed Rochdale Corporation—the [local authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_authority "Local authority") for the [Municipal Borough of Rochdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Borough_of_Rochdale "County Borough of Rochdale")—suggested plans to build a [town hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_and_town_halls "City and town halls") in which to conduct its business in May 1858.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-PMSA-3) The site of an abandoned 17th-century house known as the Wood was proposed. Six months later, in April 1860, Rochdale Corporation arranged to buy the site on the outskirts of the town centre for £4,730 (£514,000 in 2025).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-inflation-UK-7) However, plans were shelved due to lengthy negotiations and increasing land prices. In January 1864, the scheme resumed with a new budget of £20,000 (£1,860,000 in 2025).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-inflation-UK-7)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-PMSA-3)

The wood and surrounding area were cleared, but it is unknown what became of the dispossessed; there was no legal requirement for the authorities to rehouse the former inhabitants.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-cun175-13) A design competition to find a "neat and elegant building" was held by the Rochdale Corporation,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Gar81-14) who offered the winning architect a prize of £100 (£11,000 in 2025),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-inflation-UK-7) and a [Maltese cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maltese_cross "Maltese cross") souvenir. From the 27 entries received, [William Henry Crossland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Henry_Crossland "William Henry Crossland")'s was chosen.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-images-5) The Rochdale-born [Radical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radicals_(UK) "Radicals (UK)") and [Liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_(UK) "Liberal Party (UK)") statesman [John Bright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bright "John Bright") laid the foundation stone on 31 March 1866. Construction was complete by 1871 although the cost had, by then, increased beyond expectations from the projected £40,000[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Corner_stone-15) to £160,000 (£16,290,000 in 2025).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-inflation-UK-7)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Roch10-6)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Pevsner_594-16)

[![Image 9: An aged greyscale photograph is filled with an elaborate building of craggy exterior and pointed spires is bathed in daylight. In the foreground is an empty road which drops sharply into a riverbank. In the background is a church.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Rochdale_Town_Hall%2C_1874.png/250px-Rochdale_Town_Hall%2C_1874.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rochdale_Town_Hall,_1874.png)

Rochdale Town Hall as it appeared in 1874, including its original 240-foot (73 m) clock tower with wooden spire

The town hall was one of several built in the [textile towns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mill_town "Mill town") of [North West England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_West_England "North West England") following the Municipal Corporations Act 1835, but is one of only two in Greater Manchester built in the Gothic style. Between the setting of the foundation stone and the building's completion, revisions and additions were made to the original design. Money was "lavished" upon the décor and inventory, and the extra expenditure did not escape the ire of its critics.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2) The cost of the building increased year-on-year through a combination of mismanagement, overspending and "unauthorised work".[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Gar81-14) Public criticism of the high cost was aimed at Crossland and the Mayor of Rochdale, George Leach Ashworth, who oversaw the work.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-PMSA-3)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-17) Nevertheless, Rochdale Town Hall was ultimately celebrated as "a source of pride", and its completion prompted celebration and rejoicing;[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2) it transformed a "derelict and marshy riverbank in to a huge romantic Gothic plaza".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-cun175-13) The opening ceremony on 27 September 1871 was performed by Mayor Ashworth, who had been instrumental in the changes made to the building's design.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2)

In 1882 or 1883,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-18)[dry rot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_rot "Dry rot") was found in the 240-foot (73 m) high spire. On the recommendation of Rochdale's Borough Surveyor, contractors were engaged to rebuild it.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-PMSA-3) The spire was to be demolished to clear the way for a replacement. It was rumoured that the workmen who were dismantling the top section of the wooden spire may have tried to speed up the dismantling process with matches and, at 9:20 am on 10 April 1883, a blaze was discovered. Despite the efforts of volunteers and the [local fire brigade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_fire_brigades_in_the_United_Kingdom "History of fire brigades in the United Kingdom"), 100 minutes after the discovery of the fire the entire spire, including a statue of [Saint George and the Dragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_George_and_the_Dragon "Saint George and the Dragon"), had been destroyed.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-19) The cause of the fire was never established,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2) but Rochdale's fire service was criticised for taking longer to respond to the blaze than [Oldham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Borough_of_Oldham "County Borough of Oldham")'s (based 5 miles (8 km) south), despite the Rochdale Fire Brigade being based in the Town Hall.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-PMSA-3)[Alfred Waterhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Waterhouse "Alfred Waterhouse") was given the task of designing a 190-foot (58 m) stone replacement.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-PMSA-3) His work on the clock tower, which was built between 1885 and 1887[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-PMSA-3) about 15 yards (14 m) further to the east than the original,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2) shows many similarities to [Manchester Town Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Town_Hall "Manchester Town Hall"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-PMSA-3) which he also designed.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-20) The tower was opened in 1887;[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-images-5) an inscribed plaque commemorates the fire of 1883.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-PMSA-3)

On 15 January 1931, at the height of the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression_in_the_United_Kingdom "Great Depression in the United Kingdom"), the [Territorial Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territorial_Army_(United_Kingdom) "Territorial Army (United Kingdom)") was called to guard the town hall during a protest against unemployment and hunger.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-21)

In May 1938, Rochdale-born actress, singer and comedian [Gracie Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gracie_Fields "Gracie Fields") was granted [Honorary Freedom of the Borough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_Freedom_of_Boroughs_Act_1885 "Honorary Freedom of Boroughs Act 1885") for her contribution to entertainment. "When the ceremony was over, Gracie went onto the town hall balcony to receive the cheers and good wishes of the thousands of people who were packing the streets below."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-22)

Although it is not fully understood how it came to his attention, Rochdale Town Hall was admired by [Adolf Hitler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Hitler "Adolf Hitler").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-hit1-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-hit2-24) It has been suggested that military intelligence on Rochdale, or information from Nazi sympathiser [William Joyce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Joyce "William Joyce") (who had lived in [Oldham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oldham "Oldham")), brought the building to his attention. Hitler admired the architecture so much that it is believed he wished to ship the building, brick-by-brick, to [Nazi Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany") had [German-occupied Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German-occupied_Europe "German-occupied Europe") encompassed the United Kingdom. Rochdale was broadly avoided by German bombers during the Second World War.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-hit1-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-hit2-24)

The town hall closed in 2020 and conservation work began in 2021 and lasted until 2024. Alongside repairs, lifts were installed to improve access and new roof insulation was installed along with [heat pumps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_pump "Heat pump") to make it more energy efficient. The project won a [Europa Nostra Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa_Nostra_Award "Europa Nostra Award") in 2026.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-25)

## Features

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale_Town_Hall&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Features")]

### Location

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale_Town_Hall&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Location")]

At [OS Grid Reference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_national_grid_reference_system "British national grid reference system")[SD895132](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Rochdale_Town_Hall&params=53.615241_N_2.160193_W_region:GB_scale:25000) (53.6156°, −2.1594°), Rochdale Town Hall is the centerpiece of Rochdale, located in Town Hall Square to the south of The Esplanade and the [River Roch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Roch "River Roch").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-hard-26) The [Parish Church of St Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Chad's_Church,_Rochdale "St Chad's Church, Rochdale") is situated by the wooded hillside behind the Town Hall.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-hard-26) In Town Hall Square, opposite the town hall, is a statue of [John Bright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bright "John Bright"), dated 1891, and the [Rochdale War Memorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_War_Memorial "Rochdale War Memorial"). Bright was a Rochdale-born orator, pacifist and [Member of Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Parliament "Member of Parliament") for [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham_(UK_Parliament_constituency) "Birmingham (UK Parliament constituency)") known for his campaigns to repeal the [Corn Laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corn_Laws "Corn Laws") as well as his opposition to [slavery in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_United_States "Slavery in the United States") and the [Crimean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_War "Crimean War").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-rocher-27)[Touchstones Rochdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchstones_Rochdale "Touchstones Rochdale") art gallery and local studies centre is across The Esplanade.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-rocher-27)

### Exterior and layout

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale_Town_Hall&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Exterior and layout")]

[![Image 10: A large, ornate and angular taupe-coloured building on a sunny day. The building fills the image with the exception of flat, grey pavement at the building's frontage, which is dotted with people. The multi-storey building has many small slitted triangular and rectangular bays and windows across its façade, except for a dark arched entrance at ground-level. At the far end of the building is a huge clock tower topped with a triangular spire standing tall at around 15 to 20 times the height of an average adult human.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/Rochdale_Town_Hall%2C_1909.jpg/250px-Rochdale_Town_Hall%2C_1909.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rochdale_Town_Hall,_1909.jpg)

Rochdale Town Hall in 1909

The frontage and principal entrance of the Town Hall face the River Roch,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-vision-1) and comprises a [portico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portico "Portico") of three arches intersected by buttresses. Decorating the main entrance are stone [crockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crocket "Crocket"), [gargoyles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gargoyle "Gargoyle"), and [finials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finials "Finials"). Four gilded lions above a parapet around three sides of the [portico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portico "Portico") bear shields carrying the coats of arms of Rochdale Council and the [hundred of Salford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salford_(hundred) "Salford (hundred)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2)

Rochdale Town Hall is 264 feet (80 m) wide, 123 feet (37 m) deep, and is faced with [millstone grit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millstone_grit "Millstone grit") quarried from [Blackstone Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackstone_Edge "Blackstone Edge") and [Todmorden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todmorden "Todmorden").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2) Although now blackened by industrial pollution, the building has been described as a "rich example of domestic Gothic architecture".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2)[Naturalistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturalism_(arts) "Naturalism (arts)") carved foliage on the exterior recalls the style of [Southwell Minster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwell_Minster "Southwell Minster"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-images-5) and the architecture is influenced by [Perpendicular Period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Gothic_architecture#Perpendicular_Gothic "English Gothic architecture") and medieval town halls of continental Europe.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2) The building has been likened to Manchester Town Hall, [Manchester Assize Courts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Assize_Courts "Manchester Assize Courts"), the [Royal Courts of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Courts_of_Justice "Royal Courts of Justice"), and [St Pancras railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Pancras_railway_station "St Pancras railway station"), all products of the Gothic Revival architectural movement.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2) The stained glass windows, some of which were designed by [William Morris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Morris "William Morris"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-images-5) have been described as "the finest modern examples of their kind".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-RMBC43-4) At each end of the frontage is an octagonal staircase.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-vision-1)

In the words of [Nikolaus Pevsner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolaus_Pevsner "Nikolaus Pevsner"), Rochdale Town Hall has "a splendidly craggy exterior of blackened stone".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Pevsner_594-16) The building has a roughly symmetrical E-shaped plan, and is broken down into three self-contained segments: a central Great Hall and transverse wings at each end, which have variously been used as debating chambers, corporation-rooms, trade and a public hall.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-vision-1) The south-east wing used to house the [magistrates' courts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magistrates'_court_(England_and_Wales) "Magistrates' court (England and Wales)"), and the north-west wing the mayor's rooms. In the north-east is a tower. Access to the main entrance is through a central [porte cochere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porte-cochere "Porte-cochere").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-28) The façade extends across 14 [bays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_(architecture) "Bay (architecture)"), of which the Great Hall accounts for seven. On both sides, the outermost bays rise to three storeys. They flank asymmetric round-headed arcades—two to the left and three to the right, all of single-storey height—which sit below plain [mullioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mullion "Mullion") windows, balconies and ornately decorated [gables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gable "Gable").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-images-5)

[![Image 11: The view up a huge clock tower from the ground upwards. The ornate, angular tower is made of stone and appears a light-taupe colour. It fills the middle part of the image. The top of the tower has a large beige clockface, and above that, a stone spire. In the background is the sky which appears mostly as vivid azure but partly with white clouds.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Rochdale_Town_Hall_Clock.jpg/250px-Rochdale_Town_Hall_Clock.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rochdale_Town_Hall_Clock.jpg)

The [clock tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clock_tower "Clock tower") was designed by [Alfred Waterhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Waterhouse "Alfred Waterhouse"), the architect of [Manchester Town Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Town_Hall "Manchester Town Hall").

### Clock tower

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale_Town_Hall&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Clock tower")]

The original clock tower contained 13 bells, by [John Taylor & Co](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Taylor_&_Co "John Taylor & Co") of Loughborough,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Snowdon1888-29) together with a clock and [carillon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carillon "Carillon") machine (by [Gillett, Bland & Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gillett,_Bland_&_Co. "Gillett, Bland & Co.")) which played 14 different tunes on the bells.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Pickford1995-30) These were all destroyed in the 1883 fire.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-PMSA-3)

The present [clock tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clock_tower "Clock tower"), which has a stone spire, was built to replace the one destroyed in the fire. It was designed by [Alfred Waterhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Waterhouse "Alfred Waterhouse") in a similar style to one of his earlier works, the clock tower of [Manchester Town Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Town_Hall "Manchester Town Hall"). The first stone was laid by Thomas Schofield [JP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice_of_the_Peace "Justice of the Peace"), [Alderman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alderman "Alderman") and Rochdale Borough [Councillor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Councillor "Councillor"), on 19 October 1885 and the tower was declared complete on 20 June 1887, the [Golden Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Jubilee "Golden Jubilee") of [Queen Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_of_the_United_Kingdom "Victoria of the United Kingdom"). It was fitted with five bells (again by Taylor),[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Snowdon1888-29) which ring on the hour and at 15-minute intervals, and a [Cambridge-chiming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge_Chimes "Cambridge Chimes") clock by Potts & Sons, which was set going in November of that year.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Potts2006-31)

The tower rises from a [plinth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plinth "Plinth") and has four stages including the gable-headed clock stage, which is also decorated with pinnacles. A small stone spire completes the composition.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-images-5) The design of the original tower was more elaborate and 50 feet (15 m) higher than its successor, which is 190 feet (58 m) tall.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-link-2)

### Interior

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale_Town_Hall&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Interior")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Rochdale_Town_Hall_interior_29_July_2017.jpg/250px-Rochdale_Town_Hall_interior_29_July_2017.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rochdale_Town_Hall_interior_29_July_2017.jpg)

Entrance Hall

[![Image 13: See caption](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/7d/Rochdale_Town_Hall_Grand_staircase.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rochdale_Town_Hall_Grand_staircase.jpg)

Etching of the Grand staircase by [William Henry Crossland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Henry_Crossland "William Henry Crossland"), 1871

Murals in the former council chamber depict the inventions that drove the [Industrial Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_Revolution "Industrial Revolution"),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-32) and the Great Hall is adorned with a large fresco of the signing of [Magna Carta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magna_Carta "Magna Carta") by artist [Henry Holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Holiday "Henry Holiday"), although the painting is dirty.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Pevsner_59-8) Responsibility for the decoration of the interior was given to [Heaton, Butler and Bayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heaton,_Butler_and_Bayne "Heaton, Butler and Bayne"), who incorporated floor tiles that were manufactured by [Mintons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mintons "Mintons") and decorated with the local insignia and the [Royal coat of arms of the United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_coat_of_arms_of_the_United_Kingdom "Royal coat of arms of the United Kingdom").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Fawcett135-33) The stone Grand Staircase, which leads from the vestibule to the Great Hall, is decorated with stained glass; such glass windows decorate most of the Town Hall and are considered to be the finest example of the work of Heaton, Butler and Bayne.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Pevsner_595-35) The [medieval style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval_architecture "Medieval architecture") Great Hall, described by Pevsner as a room of "great splendour and simplicity",[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-Pevsner_595-35) has a [hammerbeam roof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hammerbeam_roof "Hammerbeam roof") flanked by statues of angels, in a design that resembles [Westminster Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westminster_Hall "Westminster Hall").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-RMBC43-4)

[James Jepson Binns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Jepson_Binns "James Jepson Binns") built the town hall's pipe organ in 1913; it was rebuilt in 1979 by J.W. Walker & Sons Ltd.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-36)

The town hall was [listed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Listed_building "Listed building") at Grade I on 25 October 1951.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-images-5) Such buildings are defined as being of "exceptional interest, sometimes considered to be internationally important".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-EH2-37) In February 2001, it was one of 39 [Grade I listed buildings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grade_I_listed_buildings_in_Greater_Manchester "Grade I listed buildings in Greater Manchester"), and 3,701 listed buildings of all grades, in Greater Manchester.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-IoEStats-All-38) Within the [Metropolitan Borough of Rochdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Borough_of_Rochdale "Metropolitan Borough of Rochdale"), it is one of only three Grade I listed buildings, and 312 listed buildings of all grades.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-IoEStats-GM-39)

Although the majority of local government functions now take place within [Number One Riverside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Number_One_Riverside "Number One Riverside"), Rochdale Town Hall continues to be used for cultural and ceremonial functions. For instance, it is used for the Metropolitan Borough of Rochdale's [mayoralty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor "Mayor"),[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-40)[civil registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_registry "Civil registry"),[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-43) and for formal naturalisation in [British Citizenship ceremonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_nationality_law "British nationality law").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Hall#cite_note-45)

# Reviving a municipal masterpiece

[Home](https://www.burohappold.com/) » [Projects](https://www.burohappold.com/projects/) » Rochdale Town Hall Square

## Rochdale Town Hall

#### Rochdale, UK

##### Project details

##### Client

Rochdale Development Authority

##### Architect

Gillespies

##### Duration

2019-2024

##### Services provided by Buro Happold

[Bridge engineering and civil structures](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/bridge-engineering-and-civil-structures/), [Building services engineering (MEP)](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/building-services-engineering-mep/), [Infrastructure](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/infrastructure-consulting/), [Lighting design](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/lighting-design/), [Security and public safety consulting](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/security-consulting/), [Transport and mobility](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/transport-and-mobility/)

#### Rochdale Town Hall is a grade I-listed neo-gothic building designed by William Crossland, which opened in 1871 and quickly came to symbolise the town’s rich industrial standing in the textile trade.

Over time the town hall fell into a poor state of repair and its restoration became vital in preserving the building for future generations. In 2021 work began to restore the building to its former glory. Outside, a new Town Hall Square will create a place for the community to come together.

![Image 23](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/Refurb_iconic_landmark_project_COLUMNS.gif)

 The project will see the grade I-listed town hall restored and its town hall square revitalised. 

![Image 24](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/improving-the-public-realm-communities.gif)

 The new design includes removing the road and parking in front of the town hall to create a large outdoor space and well-conceived public realm. 

![Image 25: cycle friendly design](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/Lille_Langebro_BIKE.gif)

 Our transport and mobility experts developed the plans for the successful stopping-up and pedestrianisation of The Esplanade. 

![Image 26](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/BH-remains-on-site-HARDHAT_BW.gif)

 Buro Happold’s richly multidisciplinary community of experts worked together to help deliver this technically challenging but critical regeneration project. 

### Challenge

The vision was to create the new public realm across both a former municipal car park and The Esplanade – one of the town’s key roads, which would need to be decommissioned, with traffic rerouted to provide a vibrant new public space unimpeded by passing vehicles.

The scheme, supported by a grant from the National Lottery Heritage Fund, will see the building’s historic rooms and features restored by conservation specialists Donald Insall Associates and its town hall square revitalised through extensive public realm improvements by landscape architects Gillespies.

The ambitious public realm plans encompass the whole of Town Hall Square, as well as an area behind the town hall up to Packer Spout Gardens, and sections to the side, including the island where a new Gracie Fields statue was recently unveiled.

Buro Happold was engaged to work closely with the landscape architect and wider design team to deliver expert consultancy around [civil structures](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/bridge-engineering-and-civil-structures/), [infrastructure](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/infrastructure-consulting/) and utilities, [lighting](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/lighting-design/), [security](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/advisory/security-and-risk/) and [transport and mobility](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/transport-and-mobility/).

One of the key challenges was working around an [historic building](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/heritage-buildings/), which had a range of unchartered subterranean features surrounding it, including an historic culvert discovered during initial excavations, which had to be retained and factored into the terracing design.

![Image 27](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/RochdaleTownHall_01_Gillespies-1024x683.jpg%201024w)

In 2021 work began to restore the Rochdale Town Hall neo-gothic building to its former glory, some 150 years after it was first completed. Image: Gillespies.

### Solution

The newly designed square will deliver a world-class setting for the town hall and a public space that will rival the best public squares in Europe.

The new design includes new high-quality paving, extensive pockets of greenery, tree planting, and seating areas. The square will be multi-functional and able to stage large-scale events, such as the town’s popular Feel Good festival, as well as establishing a convivial setting for the community and visitors to the town.

The improved public realm will reconnect the town hall with the grade I-listed cenotaph and memorial gardens, and other heritage and cultural points in the town, such as the river and Touchstones museum.

Our transport and mobility experts developed the plans for the successful stopping-up and pedestrianisation of The Esplanade, a busy route through Rochdale town centre. To enable this work, offsite Section 278 works were required to enable the development and ensure traffic flows are maintained through the town centre.

Our team also worked closely with the highway authority and local stakeholders to identify the key areas for improvements, including increased pedestrian crossings and sight lines at junctions, as well as the design of a new mini roundabout.

![Image 28](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/RochdaleTownHall_04_Gillespies-1024x683.jpg%201024w)

Rochdale Town Hall will be a magnificent reminder of the area’s rich history but also a warm, welcoming public space with a breath-taking backdrop for celebrations and events. Image: Gillespies.

The project will deliver a significantly improved and increased area of public realm, which includes several sections of greening and [sustainable](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/sustainability/) drainage features. We developed these in close collaboration with the landscape architect, to ensure they are fully integrated into the new public realm design.

Our team initially oversaw a number of surveys, which identified several underground constraints, some previously known about, such as the culverted River Roch, and a significant gas main, and some not, including another historic culvert and a degree of ground contamination that would need to be remediated. Identifying these constraints early allowed options to be developed for the works, which sought to balance cost with the design intent.

The [lighting](http://lighting/) strategy was also key, reflecting the multi-functional nature of the area, designed for everyday use and for large scale events. Our lighting experts provided public realm lighting designs to assist with orientation and circulation through the public space. [Facade](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/facade-engineering/) lighting accentuates architectural features, helping to maintain the architectural identity of the historic facade of the town hall.

Our [MEP](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/building-services-engineering-mep/) and utilities teams supported with the development of designs for a new low voltage network, our bridges and civil structure engineers provided insight into the [structural](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/structural-engineering/) designs for a raised terrace located at the rear of the town hall, and the seating blocks surrounding the new lawns, while our security experts delivered a video surveillance system strategy.

![Image 29](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/RochdaleTownHall_02_Gillespies-1024x683.jpg%201024w)

Buro Happold was engaged to deliver the vision of a new public realm across both a former municipal car park and The Esplanade. Image: Gillespies.

### Value

Buro Happold’s richly multidisciplinary community of experts worked together to help deliver this technically challenging but critical regeneration project.

The improved public realm will act as a centre point in Rochdale and help connect together a number of parts of the town. The redevelopment will open up the building and its external spaces to its people and visitors and create a vibrant new heart for Rochdale.

##### Services provided by Buro Happold

[Bridge engineering and civil structures](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/bridge-engineering-and-civil-structures/), [Building services engineering (MEP)](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/building-services-engineering-mep/), [Infrastructure](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/infrastructure-consulting/), [Lighting design](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/lighting-design/), [Security and public safety consulting](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/security-consulting/), [Transport and mobility](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/transport-and-mobility/)

#### Rochdale Town Hall is a grade I-listed neo-gothic building designed by William Crossland, which opened in 1871 and quickly came to symbolise the town’s rich industrial standing in the textile trade.

Over time the town hall fell into a poor state of repair and its restoration became vital in preserving the building for future generations. In 2021 work began to restore the building to its former glory. Outside, a new Town Hall Square will create a place for the community to come together.

![Image 23](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/Refurb_iconic_landmark_project_COLUMNS.gif)

 The project will see the grade I-listed town hall restored and its town hall square revitalised. 

![Image 24](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/improving-the-public-realm-communities.gif)

 The new design includes removing the road and parking in front of the town hall to create a large outdoor space and well-conceived public realm. 

![Image 25: cycle friendly design](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/Lille_Langebro_BIKE.gif)

 Our transport and mobility experts developed the plans for the successful stopping-up and pedestrianisation of The Esplanade. 

![Image 26](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/BH-remains-on-site-HARDHAT_BW.gif)

 Buro Happold’s richly multidisciplinary community of experts worked together to help deliver this technically challenging but critical regeneration project. 

### Challenge

The vision was to create the new public realm across both a former municipal car park and The Esplanade – one of the town’s key roads, which would need to be decommissioned, with traffic rerouted to provide a vibrant new public space unimpeded by passing vehicles.

The scheme, supported by a grant from the National Lottery Heritage Fund, will see the building’s historic rooms and features restored by conservation specialists Donald Insall Associates and its town hall square revitalised through extensive public realm improvements by landscape architects Gillespies.

The ambitious public realm plans encompass the whole of Town Hall Square, as well as an area behind the town hall up to Packer Spout Gardens, and sections to the side, including the island where a new Gracie Fields statue was recently unveiled.

Buro Happold was engaged to work closely with the landscape architect and wider design team to deliver expert consultancy around [civil structures](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/bridge-engineering-and-civil-structures/), [infrastructure](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/infrastructure-consulting/) and utilities, [lighting](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/lighting-design/), [security](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/advisory/security-and-risk/) and [transport and mobility](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/transport-and-mobility/).

One of the key challenges was working around an [historic building](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/heritage-buildings/), which had a range of unchartered subterranean features surrounding it, including an historic culvert discovered during initial excavations, which had to be retained and factored into the terracing design.

![Image 27](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/RochdaleTownHall_01_Gillespies-1024x683.jpg%201024w)

In 2021 work began to restore the Rochdale Town Hall neo-gothic building to its former glory, some 150 years after it was first completed. Image: Gillespies.

### Solution

The newly designed square will deliver a world-class setting for the town hall and a public space that will rival the best public squares in Europe.

The new design includes new high-quality paving, extensive pockets of greenery, tree planting, and seating areas. The square will be multi-functional and able to stage large-scale events, such as the town’s popular Feel Good festival, as well as establishing a convivial setting for the community and visitors to the town.

The improved public realm will reconnect the town hall with the grade I-listed cenotaph and memorial gardens, and other heritage and cultural points in the town, such as the river and Touchstones museum.

Our transport and mobility experts developed the plans for the successful stopping-up and pedestrianisation of The Esplanade, a busy route through Rochdale town centre. To enable this work, offsite Section 278 works were required to enable the development and ensure traffic flows are maintained through the town centre.

Our team also worked closely with the highway authority and local stakeholders to identify the key areas for improvements, including increased pedestrian crossings and sight lines at junctions, as well as the design of a new mini roundabout.

![Image 28](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/RochdaleTownHall_04_Gillespies-1024x683.jpg%201024w)

Rochdale Town Hall will be a magnificent reminder of the area’s rich history but also a warm, welcoming public space with a breath-taking backdrop for celebrations and events. Image: Gillespies.

The project will deliver a significantly improved and increased area of public realm, which includes several sections of greening and [sustainable](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/sustainability/) drainage features. We developed these in close collaboration with the landscape architect, to ensure they are fully integrated into the new public realm design.

Our team initially oversaw a number of surveys, which identified several underground constraints, some previously known about, such as the culverted River Roch, and a significant gas main, and some not, including another historic culvert and a degree of ground contamination that would need to be remediated. Identifying these constraints early allowed options to be developed for the works, which sought to balance cost with the design intent.

The [lighting](http://lighting/) strategy was also key, reflecting the multi-functional nature of the area, designed for everyday use and for large scale events. Our lighting experts provided public realm lighting designs to assist with orientation and circulation through the public space. [Facade](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/facade-engineering/) lighting accentuates architectural features, helping to maintain the architectural identity of the historic facade of the town hall.

Our [MEP](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/building-services-engineering-mep/) and utilities teams supported with the development of designs for a new low voltage network, our bridges and civil structure engineers provided insight into the [structural](https://www.burohappold.com/specialisms/structural-engineering/) designs for a raised terrace located at the rear of the town hall, and the seating blocks surrounding the new lawns, while our security experts delivered a video surveillance system strategy.

![Image 29](https://www.burohappold.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/RochdaleTownHall_02_Gillespies-1024x683.jpg%201024w)

Buro Happold was engaged to deliver the vision of a new public realm across both a former municipal car park and The Esplanade. Image: Gillespies.

### Value

Buro Happold’s richly multidisciplinary community of experts worked together to help deliver this technically challenging but critical regeneration project.

The improved public realm will act as a centre point in Rochdale and help connect together a number of parts of the town. The redevelopment will open up the building and its external spaces to its people and visitors and create a vibrant new heart for Rochdale.

# Rochdale Town Hall

Rochdale Town Hall is a grade one listed building designed by William Crossland, which opened in 1871 to symbolise the town’s rich industrial standing in the textile trade. Its ornate stylings are rivalled only by the Palace of Westminster according to Historic England.

The Rochdale Town Hall website includes:

*   [Watching a live webcam of the peregrine falcons who live in our clock tower](https://www.rochdaletownhall.co.uk/schools-learning/falcons)

*   Exploring handcrafted wedding packages and getting married at Rochdale Town Hall.
*   Discovering what to see and do at Rochdale Town Hall.
*   Hiring rooms at Rochdale Town Hall and creating memories that will last a lifetime.
*   Experiencing seasonal, locally sourced food and drink at The Martlet Kitchen.
*   How to volunteer and be a part of it.
*   Learning about the history and restoration of Rochdale Town Hall.

Visit the Rochdale Town Hall website

# Rochdale Town Hall

Rochdale Town Hall is a grade one listed building designed by William Crossland, which opened in 1871 to symbolise the town’s rich industrial standing in the textile trade. Its ornate stylings are rivalled only by the Palace of Westminster according to Historic England.

The Rochdale Town Hall website includes:

*   [Watching a live webcam of the peregrine falcons who live in our clock tower](https://www.rochdaletownhall.co.uk/schools-learning/falcons)
*   Planning your visit.
*   Experiencing the grandeur and historic rooms of Rochdale Town Hall.
*   Exploring handcrafted wedding packages and getting married at Rochdale Town Hall.
*   Discovering what to see and do at Rochdale Town Hall.
*   Hiring rooms at Rochdale Town Hall and creating memories that will last a lifetime.
*   Experiencing seasonal, locally sourced food and drink at The Martlet Kitchen.
*   How to volunteer and be a part of it.
*   Learning about the history and restoration of Rochdale Town Hall.

Visit the Rochdale Town Hall website

![Image 3: Visitors to Rochdale Town Hall.](https://www.rochdale.gov.uk/images/Town_Hall_opt.jpg)
Rochdale Town Hall is regarded as one of the UK's finest examples of Victorian Gothic architecture.

## Details

Rochdale is a large market town in Greater Manchester, located approximately 10 miles north-east of Manchester city centre and 6 miles north of Oldham. The town benefits from excellent transport links, with the A627(M) connecting directly to Junction 20 of the M62 motorway, providing easy access to Manchester, Leeds, and Liverpool. The town is also served by the Metrolink, connecting it directly to Manchester city centre and the wider tram network.

With a population of over 220,000 within the wider borough, Rochdale is undergoing major regeneration focused on town centre renewal, housing, and public realm improvements, making it an increasingly attractive destination for residents, businesses and investors.

The subject property occupies a prominent position facing Town Hall Square and the historic town hall. The pitch has developed into a F&B / leisure pitch with neighbouring occupiers including Courtyard Public House, Koko Lounge, Empire Bar and The Flying Horse.

The property is formed of two sperate demises known as 1 South Parade, currently let out to Hartley Thomas & Wright Solicitors and the former banking hall facing Town Hall Square and Fleece Street. The existing tenant in 1 South Parade holds a lease inside the L&T Act 1954 but currently holding over. They have been a longstanding tenant and are to remain in occupation.

## Details

Rochdale is a large market town in Greater Manchester, located approximately 10 miles north-east of Manchester city centre and 6 miles north of Oldham. The town benefits from excellent transport links, with the A627(M) connecting directly to Junction 20 of the M62 motorway, providing easy access to Manchester, Leeds, and Liverpool. The town is also served by the Metrolink, connecting it directly to Manchester city centre and the wider tram network.

With a population of over 220,000 within the wider borough, Rochdale is undergoing major regeneration focused on town centre renewal, housing, and public realm improvements, making it an increasingly attractive destination for residents, businesses and investors.

The subject property occupies a prominent position facing Town Hall Square and the historic town hall. The pitch has developed into a F&B / leisure pitch with neighbouring occupiers including Courtyard Public House, Koko Lounge, Empire Bar and The Flying Horse.

The property is formed of two sperate demises known as 1 South Parade, currently let out to Hartley Thomas & Wright Solicitors and the former banking hall facing Town Hall Square and Fleece Street.
