**Rochdale** ([/ˈ r ɒ tʃ d eɪ l/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_ROTCH-dayl_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key")) is a town in [Greater Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Manchester "Greater Manchester"), England, and the administrative centre of the [Metropolitan Borough of Rochdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Borough_of_Rochdale "Metropolitan Borough of Rochdale").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-GM_Gazetteer-2) In the [2021 Census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%932022_United_Kingdom_censuses "2021–2022 United Kingdom censuses"), the town had a population of 111,261, compared to 223,773 for the wider borough.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-CP-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-3) Rochdale is in the foothills of the [South Pennines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Pennines "South Pennines") and lies in the [dale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dale_(landform) "Dale (landform)") (valley) of the [River Roch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Roch "River Roch"), 5 miles (8 km) north-west of [Oldham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oldham "Oldham") and 10 miles (16 km) north-east of [Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester").

Rochdale's [recorded history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recorded_history "Recorded history") begins with an entry in the [Domesday Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domesday_Book "Domesday Book") of 1086 as _Recedham Manor_, but can be traced back to the 9th century. The [ancient parish of Rochdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_(ancient_parish) "Rochdale (ancient parish)") was a division of the [Salford Hundred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salford_Hundred "Salford Hundred") and one of the larger ecclesiastical parishes in England, comprising several [townships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Township_(England) "Township (England)"). By 1251, the town had become of such importance that it was granted a [royal charter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_charter "Royal charter").

The town became a centre of [northern England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_England "Northern England")'s [woollen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woollen "Woollen") trade and, by the early 18th century, was described as being "remarkable for its many wealthy merchants."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-Pocket_Rochdale-4) In the 19th century, it became a [mill town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mill_town "Mill town") and centre for [textile manufacture during the Industrial Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Textile_manufacture_during_the_Industrial_Revolution "Textile manufacture during the Industrial Revolution"). The town lies within the historic county of [Lancashire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancashire "Lancashire") and was a [county borough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_borough "County borough") within it before 1974.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Toponymy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Toponymy")]

The town is recorded as _Recedham_ in the [Domesday Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domesday_Book "Domesday Book") and _Rachetham_ in 1193. Variations of _Rechedham_ continue into the 13th century when the first element's termination is dropped as _Rachedam_ became _Racheham_. This change was soon followed with the suffix _-ham_ (homestead) changing to _-dale_ (wide valley).

_Rachdale_ is recorded as a name for the town in 1242, but may have been used earlier as a name for the valley, [Hundred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hundred_(county_division) "Hundred (county division)") and Parish.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-mills-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-6) The Domesday Book's rendering of the name led [Eilert Ekwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eilert_Ekwall "Eilert Ekwall") to suggest a derivation from _reced_, an obscure [Old English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_English "Old English") element meaning "hall".

Although the name of the river is still pronounced [/r oʊ tʃ/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English") (with a long vowel sound), Rochdale is pronounced [/ˈ r ɒ tʃ d eɪ l/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English") (with a shorter _o_ sound).

### Early history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early history")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/Arrow_Mill.jpg/250px-Arrow_Mill.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Arrow_Mill.jpg)

Arrow Mill is a former [cotton mill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotton_mill "Cotton mill") and [Grade II listed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grade_II_listed "Grade II listed") building in Castleton.

A [Roman road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_roads "Roman roads"), leading from [Mamucium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mamucium "Mamucium") (Manchester) to [Eboracum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eboracum "Eboracum") ([York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/York "York")), crossed the moors at [Blackstone Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackstone_Edge "Blackstone Edge").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-tde-7)

Rochdale was subjected to incursions by the [Danes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danes_(tribe) "Danes (tribe)"); the castle that [Castleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castleton,_Greater_Manchester "Castleton, Greater Manchester") is named after, and of which no trace remains, was one of twelve Saxon forts possibly destroyed in frequent conflicts that occurred between the Saxons and Danes during the 10th and 11th centuries.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-tde-7) At the time of the [Norman Conquest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Conquest "Norman Conquest"), the manor was held by a Saxon [thegn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thegn "Thegn"), Gamel. Rochdale appears in the Domesday Book of 1086 as _Recedham_ and was described as lying within the hundred of Salford and the county of Cheshire. At that time, Rochdale was under the lordship of [Roger the Poitevin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_the_Poitevin "Roger the Poitevin").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-8) Before 1212, [Henry II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_II_of_England "Henry II of England") granted the manor to [Roger de Lacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_de_Lacy_(1170%E2%80%931211) "Roger de Lacy (1170–1211)"), whose family retained it as part of the [Honour of Clitheroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honour_of_Clitheroe "Honour of Clitheroe") until it passed to the Dukes of Lancaster by marriage and then to [the Crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Crown "The Crown") by 1399.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-tde-7)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-vch-9) In [medieval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval "Medieval") times, weekly markets were held from 1250 when Edmund de Lacy obtained a grant for a market and an annual fair.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-tde-7)

[John Byron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Byron,_1st_Baron_Byron "John Byron, 1st Baron Byron") bought the manor in 1638 and it was sold by the poet, [Lord Byron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Byron "Lord Byron"), to the Deardens in 1823, who hold the title. Rochdale did not have a manor house but the _Orchard_, built in 1702 and acquired in 1745 by Simon Dearden, was the home of the lords of the manor after 1823. It was described as "a red-brick building of no architectural distinction, on the north side of the river opposite the town hall" and sometimes referred to as the _Manor House_. It was demolished in 1922.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-10)

### Industrial Revolution

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Industrial Revolution")]

Rochdale is a product of the [Industrial Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_Revolution "Industrial Revolution"),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-11) though the manufacture of woollen cloth, particularly [baize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baize "Baize"), [kerseys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kersey_(cloth) "Kersey (cloth)") and [flannels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flannel "Flannel"), was locally important as far back as the 1500s. At that time, the textile industry was rooted in the [domestic system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Putting_out_system "Putting out system") but, towards the end of the 18th century, mills powered by water started to appear.

Water power was replaced by steam power in the 19th century and local coal became important. The Deardens who were lords of the manor were among the local coal mine owners.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-12) By the mid-1800s, the woollen trade was declining and the cotton trade was rapidly growing in importance. Cotton manufacturing took advantage of new technological developments in spinning and weaving.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-13) In 1804, the [Rochdale Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Canal "Rochdale Canal") opened, providing the first link over the [Pennines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennines "Pennines") between Lancashire and Yorkshire.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-14)

During the 19th century, Rochdale became one of the world's most prominent cotton processing towns rising to prominence and becoming a major centre for [textile manufacture during the Industrial Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Textile_manufacture_during_the_Industrial_Revolution "Textile manufacture during the Industrial Revolution"). It was a [boomtown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boomtown "Boomtown") of the Industrial Revolution and was amongst the first ever [industrialised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrialisation "Industrialisation") towns.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-GM_Arch-15) By the end of the 19th century, Rochdale had woollen mills, [silk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silk "Silk") manufacturers, [bleachers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bleach "Bleach") and [dyers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dye "Dye"), though cotton spinning and weaving were the dominant industries in the community.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-17)[Turner & Newall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turner_&_Newall "Turner & Newall") was founded in Rochdale in 1871 to produce cotton-based mechanical packing, and in 1879 it became the first business in the United Kingdom to weave [asbestos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asbestos "Asbestos") cloth with power-driven machinery.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-rochdale-18)

The [socioeconomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socioeconomic "Socioeconomic") change brought by the success of Rochdale's textile industry in the 19th century led to its rise to [borough status](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_borough "Municipal borough") and it became an important regional town based upon this economic success.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-GM_Arch-15)

The [Rochdale Pioneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Pioneers "Rochdale Pioneers") opened the first [Co-operative shop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Co-operative_Group "The Co-operative Group") in Toad Lane in 1844.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-L4LRochdale-19) The reformer and [Member of Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Parliament_(United_Kingdom) "Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)"), [John Bright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bright "John Bright") (1811–1889), was born in Rochdale and gained a reputation as a leader of political dissent and supporter of the [Anti-Corn Law League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corn_Laws "Corn Laws").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-odnb-20)

### Decline of textile manufacturing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Decline of textile manufacturing")]

By the middle of the 20th century, Rochdale's economy was in decline, reflecting the broader economic situation in other textile manufacturing towns in [North West England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_West_England "North West England"). This decline was largely driven by the global availability of cheaper textile product offerings from abroad.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-Liverpool-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-22)

During the 1950s and 1960s, Rochdale's lack of a diverse economic base became very apparent, with the closure of numerous textile manufacturing facilities.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-23) Textile manufacturing did remain a major contributor to the local economy, even into the 1970s. Regionally, numerous companies still have some connection to the textile industry.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-Liverpool-21)

## Governance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Governance")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/2/2d/Rochdale_Coat_of_Arms.jpg/250px-Rochdale_Coat_of_Arms.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rochdale_Coat_of_Arms.jpg)

The [coat of arms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coat_of_arms "Coat of arms") of the former municipal borough, later the County Borough of Rochdale council, granted 20 February 1857. The arms incorporate references to Rochdale's early industries and lords.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-24)

Lying within the [historic county boundaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historic_counties_of_England "Historic counties of England") of [Lancashire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancashire "Lancashire")[since the early 12th century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Lancashire "History of Lancashire"), Rochdale was recorded in 1066 as held by Gamel, one of the twenty-one [thegns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thegn "Thegn") of the [Hundred of Salfordshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salford_(hundred) "Salford (hundred)").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-vch-9)

The ancient ecclesiastical [parish of Rochdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_(ancient_parish) "Rochdale (ancient parish)") was divided into four townships: [Butterworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butterworth_(ancient_township) "Butterworth (ancient township)"), Castleton, [Hundersfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hundersfield "Hundersfield") and [Spotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotland "Spotland"). Hundersfield was later divided into four townships: Blatchinworth, [Calderbrook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calderbrook "Calderbrook"), [Wardleworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wardleworth "Wardleworth") and Wuerdle & Wardle.

Excluding the large [chapelry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapelry "Chapelry") of [Saddleworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddleworth "Saddleworth"), which lay entirely in [Yorkshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yorkshire "Yorkshire"), the parish of Rochdale had an area of 65.4 square miles (169.4 km 2).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-vch-9)

In 1825, commissioners for the social and economic improvement of the town were established. The town became part of a [parliamentary borough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_borough "Parliamentary borough") in 1832. As there were no existing township boundaries, the commissioners and later the parliamentary constituency were deemed to cover a circular area extending three-quarters of a mile from the old market-place.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-vch-9)

Under the terms of the [Poor Law Amendment Act 1834](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poor_Law_Amendment_Act_1834 "Poor Law Amendment Act 1834"), the town became the head of Rochdale [Poor Law Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poor_Law_Union "Poor Law Union"), which was established on 15 February 1837, despite considerable local opposition.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-Workhouse-25) In 1856, Rochdale was incorporated as a [municipal borough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_borough "Municipal borough"), giving it [borough status in the United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borough_status_in_the_United_Kingdom "Borough status in the United Kingdom"), and it obtained the powers of the improvement commissioners after 1858.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-GM_Gazetteer-2)

In 1872, the remaining area of Wardleworth township and parts of Castleton, Wuerdle and Wardle, Spotland and Butterworth townships were added to the borough.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-GM_Gazetteer-2)

When the [administrative county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrative_counties_of_England "Administrative counties of England") of Lancashire was created by the [Local Government Act 1888](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Government_Act_1888 "Local Government Act 1888"), Rochdale was elevated to become the [County Borough of Rochdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Borough_of_Rochdale "County Borough of Rochdale") and was, in modern terms, a [unitary authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_authority "Unitary authority") area exempt from the administration of [Lancashire County Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancashire_County_Council "Lancashire County Council"). In 1900, most of Castleton [Urban District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_district_(Great_Britain_and_Ireland) "Urban district (Great Britain and Ireland)") was added to the borough; this [urban district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_district_(Great_Britain_and_Ireland) "Urban district (Great Britain and Ireland)") included parts of Castleton, Hopwood and [Thornham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thornham,_Greater_Manchester "Thornham, Greater Manchester") townships. In 1933, parts of Norden Urban District and Birtle with Bamford civil parish were added to the borough.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-GM_Gazetteer-2)

Under the [Local Government Act 1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Government_Act_1972 "Local Government Act 1972"), the town's autonomous [county borough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_borough "County borough") status was abolished. The municipal boroughs of [Middleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middleton,_Greater_Manchester "Middleton, Greater Manchester") and [Heywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heywood,_Greater_Manchester "Heywood, Greater Manchester") and [Littleborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Littleborough,_Greater_Manchester "Littleborough, Greater Manchester"), [Milnrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milnrow "Milnrow") and [Wardle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wardle,_Greater_Manchester "Wardle, Greater Manchester") urban districts are now part of the [Metropolitan Borough of Rochdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Borough_of_Rochdale "Metropolitan Borough of Rochdale"), one of the ten metropolitan boroughs in [Greater Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Manchester "Greater Manchester").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-GM_Gazetteer-2)

### Parliamentary representation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Parliamentary representation")]

The [Rochdale constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_(UK_Parliament_constituency) "Rochdale (UK Parliament constituency)") was created by the [Reform Act of 1832](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reform_Act_1832 "Reform Act 1832"). The constituency was held for two decades during the 20th century by [Cyril Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyril_Smith "Cyril Smith"), first of the [Liberal Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_(UK) "Liberal Party (UK)") and then of the [Liberal Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Democrats_(UK) "Liberal Democrats (UK)").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-26)

Following the [2010 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_Kingdom_general_election "2010 United Kingdom general election"), the town was represented by [Simon Danczuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Danczuk "Simon Danczuk"), who was elected as a Labour [MP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Parliament_(UK) "Member of Parliament (UK)") but was subsequently suspended and placed under investigation by the [Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labour_Party_(UK) "Labour Party (UK)").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-27)

[Tony Lloyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Lloyd "Tony Lloyd") (Labour) was elected as MP for the Rochdale constituency in the [2017 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_United_Kingdom_general_election "2017 United Kingdom general election") and represented the constituency until his death on 17 January 2024. The seat was subsequently won by [George Galloway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Galloway "George Galloway"), leader and founder of the [Workers Party of Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workers_Party_of_Britain "Workers Party of Britain"), in the [2024 Rochdale by-election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Rochdale_by-election "2024 Rochdale by-election") on 29 February; the campaign was dominated by opposition to British involvement in the [Gaza war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-28) Six months later, Galloway was defeated in the [2024 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_Kingdom_general_election "2024 United Kingdom general election") by Labour's [Paul Waugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Waugh "Paul Waugh").

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Geography")]

Further information: [Geography of Greater Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Greater_Manchester "Geography of Greater Manchester")

Rochdale is approximately 450 feet (137 m) above [sea level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_level "Sea level"), 10 miles (16 km) north-north-east of [Manchester city centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_city_centre "Manchester city centre"), in the [valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valley "Valley") of the [River Roch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Roch "River Roch"). [Blackstone Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackstone_Edge "Blackstone Edge"), [Saddleworth Moor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddleworth_Moor "Saddleworth Moor") and the [South Pennines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Pennines "South Pennines") are close to the east; on all other sides, Rochdale is bound by other towns and villages including [Whitworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitworth,_Lancashire "Whitworth, Lancashire"), [Littleborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Littleborough,_Greater_Manchester "Littleborough, Greater Manchester"), [Milnrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milnrow "Milnrow"), [Royton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royton "Royton"), [Heywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heywood,_Greater_Manchester "Heywood, Greater Manchester") and [Shaw and Crompton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaw_and_Crompton "Shaw and Crompton"), with little or no [green space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_space_reserve "Open space reserve") between them.

Rochdale's [built environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Built_environment "Built environment") consists of a mixture of infrastructure, housing types and commercial buildings from a number of periods. Its housing stock is mixed, but has a significant amount of stone or red-brick [terraced houses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terraced_house "Terraced house") from the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

The Town Hall, seven large [tower blocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tower_block "Tower block") (locally known as the [Seven Sisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Bank "College Bank"))[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-29) and a number of former [cotton mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotton_mill "Cotton mill") mark the town's skyline. The [urban structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_structure "Urban structure") of Rochdale is regular when compared to most [towns in England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_towns_in_England "List of towns in England"); its form is restricted in places by its hilly upland terrain.

Much of Rochdale's [built environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Built_environment "Built environment") is centred around a [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") in the [town centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town_centre "Town centre"), which is the local centre of both the town and borough.

## Demography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Demography")]

Further information: [Demographics of Greater Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_Greater_Manchester "Demographics of Greater Manchester")

### 2001

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2001")]

In 1971, around 4,435 (4.8%) people in Rochdale were born in the New Commonwealth.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-33)

At the [2001 UK census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_Census_2001 "United Kingdom Census 2001"), Rochdale had a population of 95,796. The population density was 11,186 inhabitants per square mile (4,319/km 2), with a 100 to 94.4 female-to-male ratio.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-34) Of those over 16 years old, 28.2% were single (never married), 44.0% married and 8.8% divorced.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-35) Rochdale's 37,730 households included 30.4% one-person, 36.6% married couples living together, 8.4% were [co-habiting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohabitation "Cohabitation") couples and 11.1% single parents with their children.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-36) Of those aged 16–74, 37.1% had no [academic qualifications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Qualifications_Framework "National Qualifications Framework"), similar to the figure for all of Rochdale, but higher than that of 28.9% in all of England.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-Stockport_MB_stats-38) In 2010, Rochdale had the highest number of [Jobseeker's Allowance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jobseeker's_Allowance "Jobseeker's Allowance") claimants in Greater Manchester, with 6.1 per cent of its adult population claiming the benefit.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-39)

### 2011

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2011")]

Rochdale had a population of 107,926, which made it about the same size as [Salford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salford "Salford") and [Stockport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockport "Stockport"); this was an increase from 95,796 in 2001. It is one of four townships in the Metropolitan Borough of Rochdale, along with [Middleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middleton,_Greater_Manchester "Middleton, Greater Manchester"), Heywood and Pennine (a township which includes [Littleborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Littleborough,_Greater_Manchester "Littleborough, Greater Manchester") and [Wardle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wardle,_Greater_Manchester "Wardle, Greater Manchester")). Rochdale is considered an Urban Subdivision by the local borough council.

### 2021

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: 2021")]

The town of Rochdale's population was enumerated at 111,261; its ethnic makeup was 57.2% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_people_in_the_United_Kingdom "White people in the United Kingdom"), 34.3% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Asians "British Asians"), 2.6% [Mixed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_(United_Kingdom_ethnicity_category) "Mixed (United Kingdom ethnicity category)"), 3.4% [Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_British_people "Black British people"), 2.1% Other and 0.5% [Arab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Arabs "British Arabs"). The town's religious makeup was 38% [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity_in_the_United_Kingdom "Christianity in the United Kingdom"), 36% [Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam_in_the_United_Kingdom "Islam in the United Kingdom"), 24.2% No Religion and has small [Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism_in_the_United_Kingdom "Hinduism in the United Kingdom"), [Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikhism_in_the_United_Kingdom "Sikhism in the United Kingdom"), [Buddhist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism_in_the_United_Kingdom "Buddhism in the United Kingdom") and [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Jews "British Jews") communities.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-CP-1)

More than 40% of children in the Rochdale borough are living in poverty.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-44)

## Landmarks

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Landmarks")]

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Town_Hall_and_Cenotaph%2C_Rochdale.jpg/250px-Town_Hall_and_Cenotaph%2C_Rochdale.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Town_Hall_and_Cenotaph,_Rochdale.jpg)

The Cenotaph stands before Rochdale Town Hall.

There are four [Grade I listed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grade_I_listed "Grade I listed") buildings in the town: the Town Hall,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-45) the Cenotaph,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-46) the [Church of St Mary in the Baum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_St_Mary_in_the_Baum,_Rochdale "Church of St Mary in the Baum, Rochdale"),[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-nhle-st-mary-47) and [St Edmund's Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Edmund's_Church,_Rochdale "St Edmund's Church, Rochdale").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-nhle-st-edmund-48)

Rochdale Town Hall is a [Victorian era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_era "Victorian era")[town hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town_hall "Town hall") "widely recognised as being one of the finest municipal buildings in the country."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-RMBC43-49) It is the ceremonial headquarters of [Rochdale Metropolitan Borough Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Borough_of_Rochdale "Metropolitan Borough of Rochdale") and houses local government departments, including the borough's [civil registration office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_registry "Civil registry").

Built in the [Gothic Revival style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_Revival_architecture "Gothic Revival architecture"), it was inaugurated on 27 September 1871. The architect, [William Henry Crossland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Henry_Crossland "William Henry Crossland"), won a competition held in 1864. The town hall had a 240-foot (73 m)[clock tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clock_tower "Clock tower"), topped by a wooden spire with a gilded statue of [Saint George and the Dragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_George_and_the_Dragon "Saint George and the Dragon"), which were destroyed by fire on 10 April 1883. A new 191-foot (58 m) stone clock tower and spire in the style of [Manchester Town Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Town_Hall "Manchester Town Hall") was designed by [Alfred Waterhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Waterhouse "Alfred Waterhouse") and erected in 1888. Art critic [Nikolaus Pevsner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolaus_Pevsner "Nikolaus Pevsner") described the building as possessing a "rare picturesque beauty."[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-Pevsner_59-50) Its [stained glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stained_glass "Stained glass") windows, some designed by [William Morris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Morris "William Morris"), are credited as "the finest modern examples of their kind."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-RMBC43-49)[_[failed verification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] It has been described as one of the United Kingdom's finest examples of [Victorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_era "Victorian era")[Gothic Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_Revival "Gothic Revival") architecture.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-NP-51)

The building came to the attention of [Adolf Hitler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Hitler "Adolf Hitler"), who was said to have admired it so much that he wished to ship the building, brick-by-brick, to [Nazi Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany") had the United Kingdom been defeated in the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-hit1-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-hit2-53)

The [Rochdale Cenotaph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Cenotaph "Rochdale Cenotaph"), a war memorial bearing four sculpted and painted flags, is located opposite the town hall. It commemorates those who died in conflicts since the [First World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_World_War "First World War"). The monument and surrounding gardens were designed by [Sir Edwin Lutyens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_Edwin_Lutyens "Sir Edwin Lutyens").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-55) It is one of eight designed by Lutyens in England. The earliest to be erected was at [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_Cenotaph "Southampton Cenotaph") in 1920; the last at [Norwich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_War_Memorial "Norwich War Memorial") in 1927. The monument is made from Cornish granite and sits on the site of a building known as Manor House, which was used as a recruiting station during World War I. It was built by Hobson Ltd of Nottingham at a cost of £12,611. It was unveiled by the Earl of Derby on 26 November 1922 and dedicated by the Archdeacon of Rochdale. It is about 10 m (33 ft) tall and the top section is a [catafalque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catafalque "Catafalque"), which includes a carving of a horizontal figure.

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/Rochdale_Town_Hall_and_Gracie_Fields_statue.jpg/250px-Rochdale_Town_Hall_and_Gracie_Fields_statue.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rochdale_Town_Hall_and_Gracie_Fields_statue.jpg)

The Dame Gracie Fields statue outside Rochdale Town Hall

Adjacent to the town hall is a statue of the late singer, comedian and actress Dame Gracie Fields. The statue was unveiled by [Roy Hudd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Hudd "Roy Hudd") on 18 September 2016. It was created by sculptor [Sean Hedges-Quinn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hedges-Quinn "Sean Hedges-Quinn"), who based the statue on Fields' look during the 1940s.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-56) The statue was the first of a woman to be unveiled in Greater Manchester in more than 100 years.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-57) It was commissioned as part of Rochdale Borough Council's wider regeneration of the town centre.

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/John_Bright_statue_in_Broadfield_Park_in_Rochdale.jpg/250px-John_Bright_statue_in_Broadfield_Park_in_Rochdale.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John_Bright_statue_in_Broadfield_Park_in_Rochdale.jpg)

The statue of John Bright MP in Broadfield Park

In Broadfield Park in the town centre, there is a statue of [John Bright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bright "John Bright") MP, a British [Radical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radicals_(UK) "Radicals (UK)") and [Liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_(UK) "Liberal Party (UK)") statesman, who is regarded as one of the greatest orators of his generation and a promoter of [free trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_trade "Free trade") policies. Bright was born in Rochdale; he became famous for his crusade to repeal Britain's [corn laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corn_Laws "Corn Laws") and his promotion of religious freedom and [electoral reform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electoral_reform "Electoral reform").

Worthy of note is a large industrial park, named the [Kingsway Business Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsway_Business_Park "Kingsway Business Park"), for which planning permission for its construction began in 2009. The complex covers an area of 420 acres (0.66 sq mi; 1.7 km 2).[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-58)

## Transport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Transport")]

[Public transport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_transport "Public transport") in Rochdale is coordinated by [Transport for Greater Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_for_Greater_Manchester "Transport for Greater Manchester") (TfGM), which owns the bus station and co-ordinates transport services in the area.

### Railway and Metrolink

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Railway and Metrolink")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/Rochdale_Railway_Station_Metrolink_stop.jpg/250px-Rochdale_Railway_Station_Metrolink_stop.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rochdale_Railway_Station_Metrolink_stop.jpg)

The Metrolink stop at Rochdale railway station

Demand from the cross-Pennine trade to support local [cotton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotton "Cotton"), [wool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wool "Wool") and [silk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silk "Silk") industries led to the building of the [Manchester and Leeds Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_and_Leeds_Railway "Manchester and Leeds Railway"). It opened in 1839 from Manchester to Littleborough and from [Normanton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normanton,_West_Yorkshire "Normanton, West Yorkshire") to [Hebden Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebden_Bridge "Hebden Bridge") in 1840. The linking section opened on completion of the [Summit Tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit_Tunnel "Summit Tunnel") in 1841.

[Rochdale railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_railway_station "Rochdale railway station") is located about a mile south of the town centre. [Northern Trains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Trains "Northern Trains") operates services on the following routes:[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-59)

*   [Leeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_railway_station "Leeds railway station") to [Manchester Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Victoria_railway_station "Manchester Victoria railway station"), via [Halifax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax_railway_station_(England) "Halifax railway station (England)") and [Bradford Interchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradford_Interchange_railway_station "Bradford Interchange railway station"); alternate services extend to [Chester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chester_railway_station "Chester railway station")
*   Leeds to [Wigan Wallgate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigan_Wallgate_railway_station "Wigan Wallgate railway station"), via [Dewsbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewsbury_railway_station "Dewsbury railway station"), [Brighouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighouse_railway_station "Brighouse railway station") and [Salford Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salford_Central_railway_station "Salford Central railway station")
*   [Blackburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackburn_railway_station "Blackburn railway station") to [Headbolt Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headbolt_Lane_railway_station "Headbolt Lane railway station"), via Manchester Victoria, [Burnley Manchester Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_Manchester_Road_railway_station "Burnley Manchester Road railway station") and [Accrington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accrington_railway_station "Accrington railway station").

The stopping service to [Manchester Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Victoria_station "Manchester Victoria station") on the [Oldham Loop line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oldham_Loop_line "Oldham Loop line") ended in October 2009, in preparation for conversion of the line to an extension of the [Metrolink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Metrolink "Manchester Metrolink") light rail system. It was deferred in 2004 on grounds of cost but, in July 2006, plans were approved for the extension from Manchester Victoria as far as Rochdale railway station; it opened on 28 February 2013, as the [Oldham and Rochdale Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oldham_and_Rochdale_Line "Oldham and Rochdale Line"). The extension to Rochdale town centre, via Drake Street and terminating opposite [Rochdale Interchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Interchange "Rochdale Interchange"), opened on 31 March 2014.

Metrolink services currently operate to [East Didsbury tram stop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Didsbury_tram_stop "East Didsbury tram stop"), via Manchester city centre, on the _Pink_ line.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-60)

### Buses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Buses")]

The borough's bus service was provided by a municipal operator, _Rochdale Corporation Transport_, which was merged into the [SELNEC Passenger Transport Executive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Manchester_Passenger_Transport_Executive "Greater Manchester Passenger Transport Executive") in 1969.

Following [deregulation of bus services across England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bus_deregulation_in_Great_Britain "Bus deregulation in Great Britain"), Rochdale was host to a number of bus operators. [First Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Manchester "First Manchester") (previously GM Buses North) established itself as the dominant company for interurban routes to destinations such as Manchester, Shaw, Oldham, Bury and Bolton. Rossendale Transport (rebranded Rosso in 2013) owned by [Rossendale Borough Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borough_of_Rossendale "Borough of Rossendale") between 1986 and 2017 until being sold to [Transdev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transdev_Blazefield "Transdev Blazefield") was the largest operator of local bus routes within Rochdale operating brands such as Rochdale Rovers, the 464 and Lakeline.

Rochdale's old bus station closed in November 2013 and was demolished in April 2014, along with the [multi-storey car park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-storey_car_park "Multi-storey car park") and municipal offices (known locally as _The Black Box_),[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-61) to make way for the new [Rochdale Riverside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Riverside "Rochdale Riverside") retail and leisure development.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-62) Its replacement, [Rochdale Interchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Interchange "Rochdale Interchange"), is located next to the council office and main library building [Number One Riverside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Number_One_Riverside "Number One Riverside") and is linked with [Rochdale Town Centre tram stop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_Centre_tram_stop "Rochdale Town Centre tram stop").

### Roads

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Roads")]

The earliest routes around Rochdale were tracks and [packhorse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Packhorse "Packhorse") routes, with a paved track over Blackstone Edge into Yorkshire that had Roman origins.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-63) As trade increased, the Blackstone Edge [turnpike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turnpike_trust "Turnpike trust") road was built in 1735.

The [M62 motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M62_motorway "M62 motorway") passes to the south of the town and is accessed via the [A627(M)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A627(M)_motorway "A627(M) motorway"), which starts at Sandbrook Park in Rochdale and runs to Elk Mill in [Chadderton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chadderton "Chadderton"). The A627(M) also provides access to Oldham.

### Canals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Canals")]

The idea for the [Rochdale Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Canal "Rochdale Canal") emerged in 1776, when [James Brindley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Brindley "James Brindley") was commissioned to survey possible routes between [Sowerby Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sowerby_Bridge "Sowerby Bridge") and Manchester.

However, it was not until 4 April 1794 that an Act of Parliament was obtained. The broad canal which linked the [Bridgewater Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgewater_Canal "Bridgewater Canal") in Manchester with the [Aire and Calder Navigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aire_and_Calder_Navigation "Aire and Calder Navigation") at Sowerby Bridge became a major artery of commerce between Lancashire and Yorkshire for cotton, wool, coal, limestone, timber and salt.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-PW-64) The Rochdale Canal has the highest concentration of canal locks in the regional northern canal system; it houses 91 locks over 32 miles (51 km).[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-65)

[Hollingworth Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollingworth_Lake "Hollingworth Lake") is part of the canal system. It was originally designed to regulate water levels and was part of the original engineering initiative. By the 1950s, the canal had fallen into general disuse and was abandoned in the 1960s, along with many other industrial areas that had supported traditional industries. The lower section from the Bridgewater Canal to the junction with the [Ashton Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashton_Canal "Ashton Canal") was restored as part of the [Cheshire Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheshire_Ring "Cheshire Ring") in 1974. The rest of the canal was restored and reopened in 2003. Local activist groups have worked to further improve the canal.

### Changing Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Changing Education")]

The structure of secondary education in Rochdale has undergone significant change since the late 20th century. During the 1960s and 1970s, pupils typically progressed through the O‑level and A‑level system, with several schools — offering academically selective streams and broad subject provision.

The national replacement of O‑levels with the General Certificate of Secondary Education (GCSE) in 1986 brought a shift toward comprehensive assessment and standardised curricula, a reform that coincided with the decline or closure of several older schools and a gradual reduction in subject specialisation.

By the early 21st century, Rochdale’s post‑16 landscape had consolidated significantly. Most secondary schools in the borough no longer maintain sixth forms, with A‑level provision now centred on Rochdale Sixth Form College, opened in 2010 as the primary provider of advanced courses for the town and wider borough. This restructuring has resulted in fewer local subject offerings than were available under the former grammar‑school and sixth‑form model, reflecting broader national trends toward centralised further‑education provision.

[Hopwood Hall College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hopwood_Hall_College "Hopwood Hall College") is a [further education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Further_education "Further education") college with a campus in Rochdale. It offers vocational courses for school leavers and adult learners, with some [higher education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_education "Higher education").

[Rochdale Sixth Form College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Sixth_Form_College "Rochdale Sixth Form College") opened in September 2010; it is the primary provider of [A-Level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-Level "A-Level") courses in Rochdale and the wider metropolitan borough. Most secondary schools in the area no longer offer [sixth form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixth_form "Sixth form") courses.

## Media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Media")]

Local news and television programmes are provided by [BBC North West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_North_West "BBC North West") and [ITV Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_Granada "ITV Granada"). Television signals are received from the [Winter Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_Hill_transmitting_station "Winter Hill transmitting station") TV transmitter.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-66)

Local radio stations are [BBC Radio Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_Manchester "BBC Radio Manchester"), [Heart North West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_North_West "Heart North West"), [Smooth North West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_North_West "Smooth North West"), [Greatest Hits Radio Manchester & The North West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest_Hits_Radio_Manchester_&_The_North_West "Greatest Hits Radio Manchester & The North West"), [Capital Manchester and Lancashire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_Manchester_and_Lancashire "Capital Manchester and Lancashire") and Rochdale Valley, a community based radio station.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-67)

Rochdale is served by a local newspaper, the _[Rochdale Observer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale\_Observer "Rochdale Observer") - founded in the early 1850s,_ and by a regional newspaper, the _[Manchester Evening News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester\_Evening\_News "Manchester Evening News")_.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-68)

## Religion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Religion")]

See also: [List of churches in Greater Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_churches_in_Greater_Manchester "List of churches in Greater Manchester")

[St Chad's Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Chad's_Church,_Rochdale "St Chad's Church, Rochdale") is a [Grade II* listed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grade_II*_listed "Grade II* listed") building.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-69) It was the mother church of the [ancient parish of Rochdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_(ancient_parish) "Rochdale (ancient parish)") and was founded before 1170, possibly on an [Anglo-Saxon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglo-Saxon "Anglo-Saxon") site. Much of the current building is the result of late [Victorian restoration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_restoration "Victorian restoration"). Other Anglican churches include the Grade I listed [Church of St Mary in the Baum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_St_Mary_in_the_Baum,_Rochdale "Church of St Mary in the Baum, Rochdale").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-nhle-st-mary-47)

[St John the Baptist Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_John_the_Baptist_Church,_Rochdale "St John the Baptist Church, Rochdale") was built in 1927 in the [Byzantine Revival style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byzantine_Revival_style "Byzantine Revival style") and is a Grade II* listed building.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-70)

[Marland Grange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marland_Grange "Marland Grange")[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-71) was a [Cistercian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cistercian_monks "Cistercian monks") grange of [Stanlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanlow_Abbey "Stanlow Abbey"), [Cheshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_monastic_houses_in_Cheshire "List of monastic houses in Cheshire"), then of [Whalley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whalley_Abbey "Whalley Abbey"). The grange was founded before 1212.

Rochdale is home to 21 mosques of [various denominations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_denominations "Muslim denominations"). Rochdale Central Masjid [Idara] is the largest of Rochdale's mosques.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-72)

## Public services

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Public services")]

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/Scout_Moor_towards_Rochdale.jpg/250px-Scout_Moor_towards_Rochdale.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Scout_Moor_towards_Rochdale.jpg)

Scout Moor Wind Farm overlooking Rochdale

[Home Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Office "Home Office") policing in Rochdale is provided by [Greater Manchester Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Manchester_Police "Greater Manchester Police") and the Rochdale Division has headquarters at Town Meadow, adjacent to the [magistrates' court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magistrates'_court_(England_and_Wales) "Magistrates' court (England and Wales)").

[Statutory emergency fire and rescue services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire_service_in_the_United_Kingdom "Fire service in the United Kingdom") are provided by the [Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Manchester_Fire_and_Rescue_Service "Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service"), which has fire stations in Rochdale, Littleborough and Heywood.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-73)

Emergency healthcare is provided by the [Northern Care Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Care_Alliance_NHS_Foundation_Trust "Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust"). The trust operates four hospitals in the North Manchester area, including [Rochdale Infirmary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Infirmary "Rochdale Infirmary") for the [NHS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Health_Service_(England) "National Health Service (England)"). Patient transport is provided by the [North West Ambulance Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_West_Ambulance_Service "North West Ambulance Service").

Rochdale Infirmary is the main hospital serving the town since the closure of [Birch Hill Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birch_Hill_Hospital "Birch Hill Hospital"), which occupied the former Rochdale Union [Workhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workhouse "Workhouse") at Dearnley, in 2007.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-Workhouse-25) New facilities were established at the infirmary as part of a restructuring of the town's healthcare services. Mental health services are found to the back of the former Birch Hill Hospital, which provides care for children and adults on both an inpatient and out-patient basis.

[Primary care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_care_trust "Primary care trust") services in Rochdale are provided by the Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale NHS Primary Care Trust. In 2006, it was announced that accident and emergency facilities at Rochdale Infirmary would be closed by 2011, leaving Oldham and Bury as the closest departments serving Rochdale.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-74) Confirmation that the unit would close was met with protest locally, including a march through the town centre.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-75)

[Waste management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waste_management "Waste management") was coordinated by the [local authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_authority "Local authority") from 1986, via the [Greater Manchester Waste Disposal Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Manchester_Waste_Disposal_Authority "Greater Manchester Waste Disposal Authority"),[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-76) and since 1 April 2018 via its representation on the [Greater Manchester Combined Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Manchester_Combined_Authority "Greater Manchester Combined Authority").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-77)

Rochdale's [distribution network operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distribution_network_operator "Distribution network operator") for electricity was [United Utilities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Utilities "United Utilities") until 2010, when its electricity subsidiary was sold to [Electricity North West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electricity_North_West "Electricity North West"). There are no [power stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_station "Power station") in the town, following the closure of [Rochdale power station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_power_station "Rochdale power station") in 1958. [Scout Moor Wind Farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scout_Moor_Wind_Farm "Scout Moor Wind Farm") was built on the high moors between [Rawtenstall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawtenstall "Rawtenstall") and Rochdale; it has 26 turbines and generates 65[MW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megawatt "Megawatt") of electricity.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-78)

United Utilities manages Rochdale's [drinking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drinking_water "Drinking water") and [waste water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waste_water "Waste water").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-UU-79) Water supplies are sourced from several reservoirs in Rochdale's outlying moorland, including [Blackstone Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackstone_Edge_Reservoir "Blackstone Edge Reservoir"), [Greenbooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenbooth_Reservoir "Greenbooth Reservoir"), [Piethorne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piethorne_Reservoir "Piethorne Reservoir"), and [Watergrove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watergrove_Reservoir "Watergrove Reservoir")[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-UU-79)

## Sport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rochdale&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Sport")]

Rochdale has two professional teams: [Rochdale A.F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_A.F.C. "Rochdale A.F.C.") ([football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football")) and [Rochdale Hornets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Hornets "Rochdale Hornets") ([rugby league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugby_league "Rugby league")); both play home games at the [Spotland Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotland_Stadium "Spotland Stadium").

Rochdale AFC were founded in 1907 and joined the [Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_League "Football League") in 1921, when the new [Football League Third Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_League_Third_Division "Football League Third Division") (North) was created.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-80) The club has never played above the third tier of the English league divisional structure and, before its promotion at the end of the 2009/10 season (their first promotion since 1969), had played continuously in the Football League's lowest division since 1974. However, the club reached the [Football League Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_League_Cup "Football League Cup") Final in 1962 and lost to [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C.").

Rochdale Hornets is one of the original twenty-two rugby clubs that formed the Northern Rugby Football Union in 1895, making it one of the world's first rugby league teams.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-81)

The town was home to former non-league football club, [Rochdale Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Town_F.C. "Rochdale Town F.C."),[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-82) but still hosts [National Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Conference_League "National Conference League") amateur rugby league club [Rochdale Mayfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Mayfield "Rochdale Mayfield"). Rochdale R.U.F.C. who play in [Bamford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bamford,_Greater_Manchester "Bamford, Greater Manchester"). There are two adult amateur football leagues: the Rochdale Online Alliance League and the Rochdale and District Sunday Football League.

Golf courses around the town include Rochdale Golf Club and Marland Golf Course, at [Springfield Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield_Park_(Rochdale) "Springfield Park (Rochdale)").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-83) The town also has a number of cricket clubs, most of which play in the Pennine Cricket League (PCL). Rochdale Sub-Aqua Club was formed in 1959 and remains active.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-84)

[Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorcycle_speedway "Motorcycle speedway") racing was staged at the [Athletic Grounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletic_Grounds,_Rochdale "Athletic Grounds, Rochdale") in 1928–30 and returned at the start of the 1970s when it provided a home for the British League Division Two [Belle Vue Aces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belle_Vue_Aces "Belle Vue Aces") juniors and [Rochdale Hornets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Hornets_(speedway) "Rochdale Hornets (speedway)"). [Peter Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Collins_(speedway_rider) "Peter Collins (speedway rider)"), who won the 1976 World Championship, was a Hornets rider.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-85) Stuart Smith[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-87) and Doug Cronshaw[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale#cite_note-88) competed in [BriSCA Formula 1 Stock Cars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BriSCA_Formula_1_Stock_Cars "BriSCA Formula 1 Stock Cars") between 1965 and 1984.
